صَامِتٌ Silent, mute, or speechless: (Msb:) pl. صَامِتُونَ (Kur vii. 192) [and صُمُوتٌ, occurring in the K in art. زم]. [Hence,] one says, مَا لَهُ صَامِتٌ وَلَا نَاطِقٌ (tropical:) [He has not mute nor vocal property; or he has not dead nor live stock]: (S, M, A:) by the former are meant gold and silver; (S, M, Msb, K;) and by the latter, camels, (S, K,) and sheep or goats, (S,) or animals: (M:) i. e. he has not aught. (S.) ―
-b2- Also, of camels, (assumed tropical:) Twenty, (O, K,) and the like. (O.) ―
-b3- And of milk, (assumed tropical:) Such as is thick. (S, O, K.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
